function: Excluded (function): learned unsupervised IC-GDBN with particle-filter inference predicts and detects LiDAR occlusion and received-power blockages and anomalies; no channel estimation, beamforming, or ISAC beams/waveforms/resources (pp. 1, 3).
notes: Reason function, shown on p. 3: "Instead of designing physical communication systems, a data-driven method ... (IC-GDBN), is introduced to predict and detect both sensor and power blockages within the ISAC framework." The abstract (p. 1) states the goal "to predict various types of LiDAR and RF power blockages, as well as to detect real-time abnormalities in an unsupervised manner". The RF branch is a scalar received-power trace computed from LiDAR/GPS positions with free-space path loss and Rician or Rayleigh fading (p. 7, Eq. (1); p. 12: "computation of received power signals using equation (1)"), so the method neither estimates nor predicts CSI, designs no beams or RIS, and allocates no ISAC beams, waveforms, or resources. Not no_learning: the dictionaries are learned by unsupervised growing neural gas clustering (p. 9). Not above_phy: no network decision is taken, and action selection is left to future work (p. 22). For the reviewer: if RF-power blockage prediction were read as channel prediction (area 2), the work would still fail the system check, since the link is a 2.4 GHz single-antenna model with scalar gains Gtx = Grx = 10 dBi (Table 1, p. 15, read from the page image) and XBee 3 Zigbee modules in the campus setup (p. 5), with no RIS. The first page holds the title "Integrated Sensing and Communication for Blockage Detection in V2X Networks" and DOI 10.1109/OJCOMS.2026.3652319, so the PDF matches its DOI.
